proposition.claim:
Equation reference: rec. Write \(\mathsf A(n,k)\) for the Eulerian number counting permutations of \(n\) letters with \(k\) descents, and put it equal to zero outside \(0\leq k<n\). Its recurrence is \[
 \mathsf A(n,k)=(k+1)\mathsf A(n-1,k)+(n-k)\mathsf A(n-1,k-1).\] The main finiteness statement fixes a number field \(K\), a finite set of excluded primes, an abelian variety \(A/K\), and an ample Neron–Severi class \(\phi\). For \(\dim A\geq4\), smooth hypersurfaces in that class with the prescribed good reduction are finite up to translation. In dimension three the theorem excludes multiples of certain specified intersection numbers.

The primitive case in Theorem 9.2 and the quotient-isogeny reduction in Corollary 9.3 distinguish an equality exclusion from a divisibility exclusion. If \(\pi:A\to A'\) is the relevant isogeny and \(\phi=\pi^*\phi'\), then \[\frac{\phi^n}{n!}=(\deg\pi)\frac{(\phi')^n}{n!}.\] Thus an exceptional primitive degree becomes a possible exceptional multiple before passage to the quotient. This explains the stronger exclusion in the final dimension-three formulation; confusing these two scopes would create a spurious objection. The sequence \(a_1=1,a_2=5,a_{i+2}=4a_{i+1}+1-a_i\) gives \(d_i=\binom{a_i+a_{i+1}}{a_i}\), with the first three values \(6,53130,216182590635135019896\), independently calculated.

Recorded check: Intended RHS A(n,1)^3/(200n); implemented ideal buffered RHS exp(-.1)*n*A(n,1)^3/200, factor n^2 discrepancy.
